text:
sam_support: FYI a customer reported intermittent 401s this morning while calling our /v1/generate endpoint. They say it happens ~1-2x per minute for a burst of traffic and then clears up. stack: our hosted API. token type: JWT from their SSO (OIDC).
anya_security: Can you paste the raw response and a minimal repro? most likely either jwks caching or alg/kid mismatch.
sam_support: Repro provided: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token_redacted>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
Response: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_token","message":"signature verification failed"}
mike_sre: logs show repeated JWKS fetches for the issuer during the incident window, but some requests still hit signature verification failures despite fresh fetch. code path: jwt.verify(token, jwks) -> sometimes raises signature error on first try, then succeeds after fetching JWKS again.
jules_eng: Huh. Could be cache race + concurrent kid rotation on their IdP. If a token is signed with kid X and our cache still has old JWKS without X, first verification fails. If we then fetch and get new keys, subsequent verification passes.
anya_security: Also saw a few logs with "token expired" errors where the token's exp was within 20s of current time. suspect clock skew too. Customer runs federated SSO — time drift plausible.
sam_support: Customer says their IdP did a key rotation around 08:12 UTC. Incident started 08:13 and ran until 08:19. They reported seeing 401 spikes during rotation window.
mike_sre: Repro steps I used locally: 1) request token signed by rotated key 2) hit endpoint concurrently with multiple threads -> ~20% of requests got 401 on first attempt, then 200 on retry.
Command used:
```bash
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate" & done; wait
```
Observed: some processes got 401 with "signature verification failed".
anya_security: Two separate root causes we're seeing: 1) JWKS cache TTL + race during key rotation 2) clock skew leading to exp/iat boundary failures. There's also one edgecase: alg mismatch. I spotted a token header with "alg": "HS256" but JWKS has RSA keys -> leads to immediate signature failure if we enforce alg checks.
jules_eng: Current JWKS caching implementation: cached per-issuer with default TTL = 24h and background refresh every 6h. On signature failure we only retry fetch if kid not found. That explains why some sign failures persist when kid is present in a freshly fetched JWKS but signature still fails (alg mismatch or transient fetch race).
anya_security: Proposed mitigations: - On signature verification failure, trigger an immediate JWKS refresh and retry verification once. - Add 30s leeway when validating exp/iat to tolerate small clock skew (configurable per-tenant). - Reject tokens where JWT header alg != key.alg (safety), but log more details so we can return clearer errors to customers.
sam_support: Draft customer message: "We observed a key rotation on your IdP during the request window which can cause transient 401s if clients or servers have cached an old JWKS. We've implemented an immediate retry + refresh on signature failure and will add a clock-leeway option; please ensure your IdP NTP is correct." Recommend Anya to review tone.
anya_security: I'll draft. Also want to add a runbook item for support: if customer sees repeated 401s during rotation, ask for token header (base64 decoded), kid, and timestamp, then check our jwks cache + fetch time.
mike_sre: Action items: - Jules: change jwks cache behavior to backoff but also allow on-demand refresh on signature error and retry verification (small change). - Jules: add metric for "jwt_verification_retries" and tag with issuer/kid/result. - Mike: add NTP healthcheck to infra monitoring and alert if host drift > 5s. - Anya: customer response + security note.
jules_eng: I'll send a PR to auth-service: update jwks client to: 1) reduce default TTL to 5m for hosted (configurable), 2) on signature verification failure do one immediate JWKS fetch+retry, 3) log full token header (safe redaction) and JWKS snapshot id. Will canary in staging, then dedicated nodes, then all.
deploy-bot: jules_eng pushed branch auth/jwks-retry -> CI passed for unit tests, staging deploy queued.
sam_support: Customer follow-up question: are we going to add retries automatically or should they re-send failed requests? They prefer not to implement client-side retries.
anya_security: We'll handle server-side retries once patch is live. Also provide guidance: ideally IdP rotates keys with overlap and sets Cache-Control headers on jwks endpoint.
mike_sre: For quick mitigation, we've increased jwks refresh rate for the issuer to 30s for the next hour while we roll the patch. That should reduce spike frequency.
jules_eng: Notes for PR: code snippet for retry path:
```js
try { verify(token, cachedJwks); } catch (err) { if (err.message.includes('signature') || err.message.includes('kid not found')) { const fresh = await jwksClient.fetch(issuer); cache.set(issuer, fresh); verify(token, fresh); } else throw err; }
```
Also using jsonwebtoken verify with { clockTolerance: 30 } for leeway.
anya_security: After rollout, add test harness: simulate key rotation + concurrent verification to validate retry logic. Also check perf impact.
sam_support: ETA for patch??
jules_eng: aiming for canary in staging today, prod roll tomorrow morning with ramp.
anya_security: I'll prepare postmortem note and a KB article for support with repro steps, queued as internal doc.
mike_sre: closing loop: once patch is live we should reach out to affected customers proactively.
sam_support: thanks everyone. I'll ping once customer confirms reduced errors. :thumbsup:
